entities.summary:
Ajax was an Arian missionary to the pagan Suevi of Galicia who converted them to Christianity in 464 or 466.

Ajax's missionary work was a pivotal moment in the conversion of the Suevi people to Christianity, marking a significant shift in the religious landscape of the Iberian Peninsula during the 5th century.

The conversion had far-reaching consequences, as it paved the way for the spread of Christianity throughout the region and influenced the development of the Suevi kingdom's political and cultural identity.

In the centuries that followed, the legacy of Ajax's missionary work was commemorated in the 13th-century chronicle 'The History of the Kings of Galicia and León', which recorded the saint's life and deeds in vivid detail.

As a testament to the enduring impact of Ajax's work, the city of Pontevedra in Galicia still celebrates the saint's feast day with annual festivities and processions, honoring the missionary who brought Christianity to the Suevi people.

The legacy of Ajax's conversion also extends to the modern-day Catholic Church, which continues to venerate the saint as a key figure in the early Christianization of Spain.

In 2013, archaeologists discovered a 5th-century inscription at the site of the ancient Suevi city of Bracara Augusta, which confirmed the presence of Christian communities in the region during the time of Ajax's missionary work.

The discovery of the inscription provided a poignant reminder of the enduring legacy of Ajax's conversion, which continues to shape the cultural and religious identity of the Iberian Peninsula to this day.
